prompt:
Create an internal rough film storyboard page on white paper. Exactly 12 separate panels in FOUR COLUMNS and THREE ROWS, read left to right then top to bottom. Overall page portrait 3:4; each camera panel portrait 9:16. Keep every scene fully inside its own rectangular panel, with generous white gutters. Use only loose monochrome pencil contour sketches, a few light grey shadows and simple recognizable main props. Human silhouettes have ordinary simplified human head, torso and limb proportions, NOT round-head stick figures or whiteboard stick glyphs. No polished cartoon rendering, color, realistic likeness or final character design. A wooden-boy puppet is recognizable through a short nose, feathered cap and jointed elbows/knees. The recurring producer is a simple suited adult man with side-parted hair. Equipment and clothes broadly fit the 1940s. Only exact panel IDs appear in the outer margin of each panel; no other readable text, numbers, labels, money symbols, signs, captions or slogans inside any scene. No decorative montage, merged panels, duplicate subjects or omitted panels. Show one clear action or resolved state per panel. These are original composition sketches, not archival photographs or final production artwork.

S25: Close film canister return. One plain hand sets a film canister beside a projector; wordless wooden-boy film artwork visible on the lid. No number/date.
S26: Wide cinema attendance. The same father, mother and child now approach the ticket booth together; exactly three people, no crowd.
S27: Extreme close ticket tear. Exactly two hands tear one unprinted admission ticket at the cinema entrance; no faces or readable numbers.
S28: Close cash accumulates. One plain money bag is set beside an expanding coin pile on the table; no text or humans.
S29: Medium money growth. Several plain money bags now fill most of the same receipts table; no person, no numerical label.
S30: Wide overflowing money. The table is filled with plain bags and coin piles, with one bag on the floor. No people or markings. Clear source wealth metaphor.
S31: Extreme close spill. A few coins roll from the table edge into a waiting pile; no person or word.
S32: Medium complete cash pile. The bags and coins settle into a large stable pile around the table; no people.
S33: Close producer reaction. Exactly one suited producer looks toward the money with an amused, surprised expression. Simplified human features only.
S34: Close campaign artwork. The same wordless poster of wooden boy and round-eared mouse in military tunics is seen beside a blank film reel; only two drawn figures, no humans.
S35: Medium producer sits. Exactly one suited producer sits on a playful throne made of money bags. Satirical source wealth metaphor, no literal historic event claim.
S36: Wide resolved wealth tableau. Exactly one suited producer sits still on the money-bag throne with settled coins around him; no posters, other people, captions, buttons or slogans.

Make all 12 prescribed compositions distinct and immediately readable. Every subject count above matters. Preserve the two printed cartoon figures as printed prop artwork, not extra living people. Give panels clear framing contrast without adding unrequested characters. All page content stays grayscale.
